fatal_errors: The proposed Al-for-Hf substitution does not reconstruct the demonstrated 4.2 at.% Cr addition or the approximately 3.8–4 vol.% reticulated Laves-phase mediator.

Retention of a single-phase BCC structure and absolute high-temperature strength after Al substitution is assumed without supporting evidence; the cited evidence also warns that Al additions generally reduce plasticity.
The loading mode is left as tensile or compression, preventing a controlled comparison with the compression-tested baseline.
The falsification rule incorrectly rejects strength improvements greater than 5%, even though the requirement is to avoid sacrificing performance rather than to prohibit improvement.
explanation: The hypothesis directly addresses density reduction and proposes a testable light-element substitution, so it is a scientifically plausible alternative. E1 and E3 support the general strategy of adding Al to lower RHEA density, but they do not establish that replacing Hf in HfMoTaTiZr will preserve its approximately 1600 MPa room-temperature and 855 MPa high-temperature yield strengths. It misses the target intervention and mechanism: Cr incorporation, lattice contraction and solid-solution hardening, plus an interconnected Cr2(Ti,Zr,Hf,Ta) Laves network that impedes cracks and compensates plasticity. It also omits the target increase in fracture strain and the relevant morphology-dependent boundary. The experiment has numerical rejection thresholds, but its broad 10–20 at.% composition range, unspecified loading mode, absence of phase/morphology and lattice-parameter measurements, and lack of strain-rate or environmental controls weaken discrimination.
